title: A page from a text file

terminal.description: The page runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. The shell is here if you want to look around the files.

tasks.title: Start the page and wrap it
tasks.description:
Give `index.html` the two things every page starts with.

- The doctype that says this is a modern HTML page comes first, above everything else. Only a comment may sit over it.
- An `html` element wraps everything after it: its opening tag right after the doctype, its closing tag at the very end of the file.
- The opening `html` tag says the page is in English.

The check reads the file for the doctype and both `html` tags and where they sit, and looks for the language on the root element.
nextSteps: Read "The skeleton of every page" in the lesson.
Write the doctype above everything else, below the comment if you like.
Open the `html` element after it and close it on the last line.
Add the attribute that names the language, save and press Check.
hints: The doctype is not an element. It is one short line that starts with `<!` and ends with `>`.
The root element is named after the language itself. It is the one element every other element sits inside.
The language goes in an attribute on the opening tag, written as a name, an equals sign and a value in quotes. The value for English is two letters.

tasks.title: Give the page a head and a title
tasks.description:
Add a `head` element as the first thing inside `html`. In it:

- a `meta` element that sets the character set to UTF-8
- a `title` whose text is `Kilnworth Pottery`, so the browser tab shows the studio's name

The check reads the file for the opening and closing `head` tags and where they sit, then looks for the character set and the title inside the head.
nextSteps: Read "What goes in the head" in the lesson.
Open and close a `head` element right after the opening `html` tag.
Add the character set inside it, then the title.
Save and look at the top of the Browser panel, then press Check.
hints: Nothing in the head shows on the page. You will see the title at the top of the Browser panel, beside the file name.
The character set is an element with no content and no closing tag. Its only job is one attribute.
The meta element has a `charset` attribute set to `utf-8`. The title is an ordinary pair of tags with the studio name between them.

tasks.title: Put the words in the body
tasks.description:
Add a `body` element after the head and move Dilys's words into it.

- `Kilnworth Pottery` is the one main heading of the page.
- The line about Saddler Street and the line about the kettle are two paragraphs, one each.
- No words are left loose in the body, outside an element.

Keep her words as they are. The check reads the file for the `body` tags and makes sure every paragraph closes, then looks for the heading, the two paragraphs and any loose text.
nextSteps: Read "Headings and paragraphs" in the lesson.
Open a `body` after the head and close it just before the closing `html` tag.
Wrap the studio name in the main heading element.
Wrap each of the two lines in a paragraph, save and press Check.
hints: Everything you can see on the page lives in the body. The head and the body sit side by side inside `html`.
The main heading is level one of six heading elements. Paragraphs have a one-letter element.
You need an `h1` around the name and a `p` around each of the two lines, all inside `<body>` and `</body>`.
